rule.title: used to: past habits
rule.explanation:
«Used to» + verbo describe hábitos o situaciones del pasado que ya no son así. Es igual para todas las personas:
- «We used to go to the beach every summer.» (íbamos a la playa todos los veranos; ahora no)
- «I / she / they used to live in Valencia.»
- «I used to have long hair.»

La negativa es «didn't use to» (sin d) y la pregunta, «Did you use to…?»:
- «I didn't use to like coffee.»
- «Did you use to play the guitar?»

Para algo que pasó una sola vez se usa el past simple, no «used to»:
- «My dad gave me a guitar when I was eight.»

Ojo: «used to» solo habla del pasado. Para un hábito de ahora se usa el present simple con «usually»: «I usually walk to work» (nunca «I use to walk»).

rows: I used to live by the sea.
I didn't use to like coffee.
Did you use to play the guitar?
My dad gave me a guitar.

sets.instructions: Completa con «used to», «use to» o la forma correcta del verbo.

items.sentence: When I was a child, we ___ go to the beach every summer.
answers: used to

items.sentence: Sam didn't ___ practise the guitar very much.
answers: use to

items.sentence: Did you ___ live near the sea?
answers: use to

items.sentence: My dad ___ me a guitar when I was eight. (give, una vez)
answers: gave

answers: used

answers: used

answers: use
